subject: Aegis Health renewal - multi-year commit structure & staged ramp approval
messages:
From: Cara Nguyen <cara@aegishealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aegishealth.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-year discount and staged ramp question

Hi Priya,

Following our renewal planning workshop last week, the finance team asked me to formalize Aegis's ask for the 3-year commitment. High level: we're willing to commit to a 3-year minimum $1.2M ARR equivalent if Redwood can support a staged ramp and a meaningful term discount up front.

Key constraints:
- Year 1 usage will be ~40% of committed volume as we pilot across two products.
- Year 2 we expect ~85% of that commit as we expand; Year 3 should be at or above 100%.
- Procurement needs predictable invoicing and a true-up mechanism at year boundaries.

Target economics: we are looking for ~30% blended discount versus list over 3 years (or equivalent up-front credit). If you have options with split billing or front-loaded credits that protect both sides during the ramp, we can move quickly.

Can you send a proposal with: staged ramp, true-up window/process, and an invoicing recommendation (annual vs quarterly vs front-loaded)? We need procurement and legal visibility by June 22.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if it's easier.

— Cara
Director, Cloud Platform
Aegis Health

Attachment: Aegis_Renewal_Notes.pdf (customer-provided)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Cara Nguyen <cara@aegishealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-year discount and staged ramp question

Hi Cara — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. We can support a staged ramp + true-up; below is an initial commercial construct for your procurement team to review.

Proposal (high level)
- Term: 36 months commit, target committed spend $3.6M total (annualized $1.2M).
- Ramp profile: Yr1 40% of committed units, Yr2 85%, Yr3 100%.
- Discounting: two options —
  Option A (upfront credit): 32% blended effective discount applied as a front-loaded credit on Year 1 invoice; annual true-up at each anniversary.
  Option B (annual discount sweep): 28% on Year 1 bill, 30% Year 2, 32% Year 3 with true-up settled in Yearly reconciliation.
- Invoicing: prefer annual or annual-with-quarterly-draw (customer choice).
- Protections: 60-day true-up window; mid-term usage protections with fixed per-token floor if usage falls below 30% of commit in Year 1.

I'll loop in finance and pricing to confirm margin/approval for Option A vs B and return a clean term sheet and a simple spreadsheet you can share with procurement.

If that direction looks reasonable, I can prepare a DocuSign-ready term sheet by June 14. Want to do a 30-min call to walk procurement through the mechanics?

Best,
Priya
Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: aegis_commit_model_v3.xlsx (pricing model)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Aegis Health - multi-year ask — approval request

Hi team — looping you in for an approval path. Customer is asking for staged ramp protection + a blended ~30% discount. I modeled two options in the attached:
- Option A: 32% blended via Year 1 front-loaded credit (accelerates revenue deferral but simplifies customer cashflows).
- Option B: Increasing discount by year, lower front-loaded liability.

Itemized asks:
- Pricing/Finance (Karthik): can we support Option A with the proposed credit without breaking target gross margin? If not, what is the maximum blended % we can approve on a standard deal desk authority?
- Sales leadership (Marissa): recommend approval threshold for renewals >$3M total ARR equivalent and any pref on billing cadence.
- Legal (Ben): any procurement redlines I should pre-clear (SLA credits, data residency language, true-up windows).

Attachments: aegis_commit_model_v3.xlsx, pricing_breakdown.csv, term_sheet_AEG_3yr_v1.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump into a quick call.

— Priya

> On Jun 1, 2027, at 12:05 PM, Priya Natarajan wrote:
> > [sent to customer with initial proposal summary]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Aegis Health - multi-year ask — approval request

Priya — reviewed the model and the ask. Short answer: we can support a one-time blended 31.5% effective discount if the customer commits to:
- 100% of the $3.6M committed annualized amount in contractual language (true contract value).
- Annual true-up with a 60-day settlement and pre-agreed make-good credits if shortfall >10% in Year 1.
- Customer agrees to annual billing (preferred) or annual-with-quarterly-draw.

Trade-offs and recommendations:
- Option A (front-loaded credit) causes revenue deferral and increases month 0 liability; finance is comfortable up to ~32% blended for this cohort if we get full contract language and a top-level approval.
- If Procurement insists on lower up-front cash flow impact for Redwood, push Option B and accept ~29% blended.

Marissa: recommend we approve up to 32% blended for named strategic customers in Healthcare vertical (Aegis fits). Ben: please flag any legal showstoppers on true-up mechanics and SLA offsets.

— Karthik
Head of Pricing Strategy

> On Jun 8, 2027, at 09:45 AM, Priya Natarajan wrote:
> > [internal ask and attachments]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Aegis Health - multi-year ask — approval request

All — legal has reviewed the term sheet draft. A few quick notes:
- True-up window: 60 days is fine but we should include a single arbitration/EScalation step for disputes to avoid procurement stalls.
- SLA credits: we should cap operational credits tied to SLA at 10% of monthly invoice; otherwise procurement will push back.
- Billing terms: if customer requests front-loaded credits, we need explicit language around how credits are applied and an audit right for usage reporting.

Assuming pricing team is comfortable, no legal blockers. Approve the term sheet with the 31.5% blended (rounded to 32% in the external doc) and include the three bullets above.

— Ben
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Cara Nguyen <cara@aegishealth.com>, procurement@aegishealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Multi-year discount and staged ramp question

Hi Cara — thanks for the patience. Good news: Redwood can offer a commercial that meets your ramp protection needs. Summary of approved offer below.

Approved commercial (final)
- Term: 36 months; committed value $3.6M (annualized $1.2M).
- Discount: 32% blended effective discount (presented as Option A in earlier note) applied as a Year 1 front-loaded customer credit.
- Ramp/true-up: Yr1 40% expected usage, Yr2 85%, Yr3 100%. Annual true-up with 60-day settlement window; make-good credits if Year 1 actual usage <30% of commit.
- Billing: customer may elect Annual billing or Annual-with-quarterly-draw.
- Protections: SLA credit cap at 10% monthly invoice; arbitration step for disputes on usage reconciliation; Redwood audit right for usage reporting related to credits.

Next steps
1) I'm attaching the clean term sheet and pricing model for procurement (term_sheet_AEG_3yr_v1.pdf; aegis_commit_model_v3.xlsx).
2) If approved on your side, I'll send a DocuSign agreement (link below) — we aim to have countersigned agreement by June 25 to meet your internal gating.
3) Procurement / Legal: let me know any redlines within 3 business days and we'll try to move quickly.

DocuSign draft: https://www.docusign.com/agreements/3YR-AEG-V1

Happy to set a 30-min call to walk the team through the mechanics tomorrow morning PST if useful.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

— Priya
Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: term_sheet_AEG_3yr_v1.pdf, aegis_commit_model_v3.xlsx, pricing_breakdown.csv
